page: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MSv2 family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8280L processor featuring 416 vCPUs across 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz and is configured with an extensive 5700.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 13.7 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 8389 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is positioned in the bottom 25% across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, and single-threaded gzip compression is similarly limited. Conversely, multi-core execution is highly efficient, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all registering in the top 10% globally. Memory bandwidth is also a key strength, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching 19406.65 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 767.47 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier.

Given its massive memory footprint and high multi-core throughput, the M416s_v2 is designed for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, and heavy data-warehousing workloads. This is supported by its top-tier Redis SET performance of 260.18 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 139.05 GB/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile represents a highly specialized, high-density resource allocation. While single-threaded tasks are inefficient on this platform, the consolidation of massive datasets into a single memory space reduces the overhead of distributed clustering, making it qualitatively efficient for centralized, memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is a memory-optimized server from the MSv2 family, featuring 416 vCPUs (208 physical cores) powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors running at 2.7 GHz. It is equipped with 5700.0 GB of RAM and 8389 GB of local storage, with no GPUs. Benchmarks indicate a significant performance tradeoff: single-core metrics are weak, placing in the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core performance and memory bandwidth rank in the top 10% globally. This includes a multi-core stress-ng score of 376,443.61 and cached memory bandwidth of 19,406.65 GB/sec. The server is highly optimized for massive in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, and data warehousing, where its high memory density and parallel processing capabilities offset its lower single-threaded efficiency.
